content:
If I build a large project, say mathlib, and measure the total size of all .json files in .lake, it takes a significant fraction of the disk space.
On the other hand, these files can be compressed without much difficulty.
Have anyone looked into this?
*.setup.json files in .lake are temporary and persist primarily for debugging purposes. You can delete them if they are taking up too much space.

what do you think about automatically cleaning them up at appropriate time?
Part of the reason is, suppose .lake is 10GB, .setup.json takes 4GB, and the machine only have 8GB left, it's impossible to build it and delete the .setup.json afterwards. Another part is it may be better to have the default behavior being reasonable for most users, who would have never come across this conversation.
:thinking: I'll look into it.
